title: Communications During Network and Power Outages
summary: Preserving device battery, alternative communication channels, broadcast radio, and digital landline limitations.
content:
1. BATTERY DISCIPLINE:
- Immediately switch phones to 'Low Power Mode' / 'Battery Saver'. Lower screen brightness, disable Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, location services, and background apps.
- If in a household, turn off all phones except one. Rotate usage between devices to conserve battery.
- Charge phones safely via car 12V USB adaptors outdoors in open air (never run car engines inside closed garages).

2. SMS OVER CALLS:
- When cellular networks are overloaded, text messages (SMS) transmit far more reliably than voice calls because they require minimal bandwidth.
- Keep text messages brief and factual (e.g. 'Safe at home, battery low, phone off until 18:00').

3. EMERGENCY ROAMING:
- If your primary mobile network provider loses signal, 999 / 112 calls automatically roam onto any available working network in the area.

4. BROADCAST RADIO:
- Keep a battery-operated or wind-up FM/AM radio accessible for public emergency broadcasts.
- Tune to BBC Radio London on 94.9 FM (verify locally) or national emergency broadcasts on BBC Radio 4 (92-95 FM / 198 LW - verify locally).

5. DIGITAL LANDLINE LIMITATION:
- Note that modern UK landlines (Digital Voice / VoIP) rely on home broadband routers and will NOT work during a mains power cut without a dedicated battery backup unit.

6. FAMILY MEETING PLANS: Pre-agree on an offline family meeting location and maintain a written paper copy of all essential phone numbers.
